invented.quote: The Long Dark Season: Keep the Light Burning
invented.why: The brief does not give a title or subtitle for the board game.

invented.quote: The supply boat won't come again until spring. The oil has to last, the children have to eat, and ships need the light every night.
invented.why: The brief only states that the game is about seeing a lighthouse keeper's family through a winter, without mentioning a supply boat, oil, children, or ships.

invented.quote: on an island at the edge of the map.
invented.why: The brief does not specify that the lighthouse is located on an island or at the edge of the map.

invented.quote: Each turn you decide what gets done today and what has to wait: fixing the lamp, rationing the stores, caring for someone who's sick, or going out in the storm.
invented.why: The brief does not describe the turn structure, time scale, or specific actions players take in the game.

invented.quote: No two winters play out the same, and the hardest choices often have nothing to do with the light.
invented.why: The brief does not state anything about the game's replayability or the nature of its hardest choices.

invented.quote: Tested at hundreds of tables, one game at a time
invented.why: The brief states there were 140 playtest sessions, which is not hundreds of tables.

invented.quote: families, first-timers, longtime hobby gamers and solo players.
invented.why: The brief only states that about 60 different people playtested the game, without describing their backgrounds or how they played.
The brief does not state that changes were made to the game after every playtest session.
The brief states the creator took the game to two conventions, but does not state the reason or that strangers played it.

invented.quote: **The rest:** platform and payment fees, plus a reserve for freight and surprises
invented.why: Wait — the factory quote ($17,400) plus shipping 1,500 copies at $9 ($13,500) equals $30,900, which already exceeds the $28,000 goal, and the brief says nothing about platform fees, payment fees, freight, or a reserve.

invented.quote: The goal covers what it takes to produce the game and get it to you. It doesn't include any pay for me.
invented.why: The brief does not state whether the creator is taking any pay from the campaign or if the goal fully covers production and fulfillment.

invented.quote: If we go past the goal, the extra money gives the project a safety margin before any stretch goals.
invented.why: The brief does not mention stretch goals or how funds raised beyond the $28,000 goal will be used.

invented.quote: To lower that risk, I locked in the manufacturing quote before launch, budgeted shipping per copy, and built a reserve into the goal.
invented.why: The brief mentions a factory quote and a shipping cost, but does not state that the quote is locked in or that a financial reserve is built into the goal.

invented.quote: This game has been through four winters of playtesting.
invented.why: The brief only states that playtesting has been happening 'since 2023', which does not establish that it has been through four winters.
